findings.title: No cache re-check after taking the write lock
findings.body: Callers that find the cache empty all queue on `Lock()`. Each one then runs the full load (manifest file read, plus the CDN URL lookup) one after another, because nothing re-checks `entryPointAssetsCache` once the lock is held. At cold start, or after a failed load that leaves the cache nil at line 69, N concurrent requests do N reads. Re-check the cache under the lock when `cfg.Env != setting.Dev`. In Dev mode the cache is deliberately bypassed, so every request takes the exclusive lock and reads the file serially. That is correct, but it serializes page loads in dev.

contracts.action: Guard the global entryPointAssetsCache with an RWMutex in GetWebAssets
contracts.equivalent_path: The previous unsynchronized read and write of the global cache in the same function.
contracts.before_after: Before, the cache was read and written with no lock, which is a data race. Now reads take RLock and the load and write take Lock. The cache hit path is unchanged. The miss path is serialized but does not re-check the cache.
contracts.visible_effect: The race is gone. Requests hitting a cold cache wait on the lock and then each reload the assets.
contracts.failure_mode: If the load fails, the cache is set to nil and the error is returned, as before. The deferred Unlock releases the lock on every path, including panics, so there is no deadlock.

summary: The mutex change correctly removes the data race. The only issue is that the write path does not re-check the cache, so concurrent cold-start requests each reload the manifest. Dev mode also serializes every request on the exclusive lock.
